@graph.keywords: SOC 2 compliance services India, SOC 2 audit India, SOC 2 readiness assessment, SOC 2 Type I, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 2 consulting, AICPA Trust Services Criteria

acceptedAnswer.text: SOC 2 is an attestation report issued by an independent AICPA-licensed CPA firm after evaluating a service organization's controls against the Trust Services Criteria (TSC): Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality and Privacy. Indian SaaS, cloud and IT services companies commonly need it to sell to enterprise customers in the USA, UK, UAE and other markets.

mainEntity.name: Is SOC 2 mandatory for companies in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: SOC 2 is not a legal requirement in India. It is a customer-driven standard: enterprise buyers, especially in the USA and UK, often make a SOC 2 report part of vendor due diligence, so it becomes a commercial necessity for companies that sell to them.

mainEntity.name: Does ISECURION issue the SOC 2 report?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A SOC 2 report is issued by an independent AICPA-licensed CPA firm. ISECURION prepares your organization for the audit: scoping, gap assessment, control implementation, documentation, evidence readiness and coordination with the CPA firm until the report is issued.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between SOC 2 Type I and Type II?

acceptedAnswer.text: Type I assesses the design of controls at a point in time. Type II assesses operating effectiveness across a period, typically 3–12 months. Most enterprise buyers, especially in the USA and UK, require Type II. Many Indian companies start with Type I and achieve Type II within 6–12 months.

mainEntity.name: How long does a SOC 2 audit take?

acceptedAnswer.text: SOC 2 Type I can typically be achieved 6–10 weeks after remediation is complete. Type II requires a review period of 3–12 months of operating evidence before the audit window closes. Timeline depends on your starting maturity. ISECURION provides a timeline estimate as part of the free gap snapshot.

mainEntity.name: What affects the cost of SOC 2 compliance in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on scope: the number of Trust Services Criteria included, the systems and locations in scope, your current control maturity, team size and the CPA firm chosen for the audit. ISECURION scopes your requirement first through a free gap snapshot and then provides an itemized quote for the readiness work.

mainEntity.name: Do we need ISO 27001 before pursuing SOC 2?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Many companies pursue SOC 2 as their first compliance framework. If you want both ISO 27001 and SOC 2, ISECURION harmonizes controls to minimize duplication and effort, which is a popular choice among SaaS companies expanding globally.

mainEntity.name: Which tools and cloud platforms does ISECURION support?

acceptedAnswer.text: ISECURION supports AWS, Azure, GCP, Okta/Entra, Jira, GitHub/GitLab, CrowdStrike/Defender, Datadog and most modern SaaS stacks. We adapt to your environment rather than asking you to change tools to fit our methodology.

mainEntity.name: Does ISECURION provide SOC 2 services across Indian cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We support companies in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata, Delhi NCR, Kochi and elsewhere in India through on-site or remote engagements.

mainEntity.name: Does ISECURION provide SOC 2 services outside India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Engagements for companies in the USA, UK, UAE, Australia and Singapore are delivered remotely and scheduled around your time zone. We coordinate with AICPA-licensed CPA firms on your behalf.

@graph.name: How ISECURION takes your organization from SOC 2 scoping to a CPA-issued report
@graph.description: ISECURION's 5-phase process to get your organization SOC 2 ready and supported through the audit.

step.name: Scoping and Consultation
step.text: Define in-scope products, systems, vendors, locations and Trust Services Criteria (TSC).

step.name: Readiness and Gap Assessment
step.text: Compare existing controls against SOC 2 expectations and create a prioritized remediation plan.

step.name: Remediation and Control Implementation
step.text: Implement access management, change management, backup, incident response, vendor and SDLC controls.

step.name: Evidence Collection and Documentation
step.text: Build an audit-ready evidence pack including logs, tickets, policies, risk register and configurations.

step.name: Audit Support and Ongoing Compliance
step.text: Coordinate with the CPA firm, respond to PBC lists and maintain controls after the report is issued.
